key_insight: A polymorphic AB2O6 high-entropy oxide photocatalyst combined with microalgae sacrificial scavenging greatly boosts solar-driven CO2 conversion to CO and CH4.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a more sustainable reactor strategy that couples carbon capture by microalgae with enhanced photocatalytic reduction, improving the practicality of CO2-to-fuels systems.
method: Use layered perovskite/pyrochlore bi-polymorphy to support CO2 chemisorption, polarization, and charge transport
Compare photocatalysis with no sacrificial agent, microplastics, and microalgae under solar-driven CO2 conversion
evidence_signal: Compared with the HEO-only system, adding microalgae increased CO and CH4 production by about 10-fold and 4-fold, respectively, according to the abstract.
watch_item: The abstract does not provide long-term stability, microalgae handling, or scalability data, which are critical for real deployment.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
